description: Project NOMAD is an offline-first knowledge and education server. Wikipedia, thousands of books, courses, maps, and optional local AI, all running on hardware you own with no internet required.

summary.one_liner: Project NOMAD is a self-hosted, offline-first knowledge and education server that bundles offline Wikipedia, courses, maps, tools, and optional local AI, managed through a browser-based Command Center running on Docker.
summary.what_it_does: Project NOMAD is a management UI (the "Command Center") and API that installs and orchestrates containerized tools via Docker, all accessed through a web browser. Its bundled capabilities include an offline Information Library (Wikipedia, medical references, ebooks) via Kiwix, an education platform with Khan Academy courses and progress tracking via Kolibri, downloadable offline regional maps via ProtoMaps, and CyberChef for encryption, encoding, and data analysis. It also provides FlatNotes for local markdown notes and a hardware System Benchmark with a community leaderboard. The optional AI Assistant offers local chat through Ollama or OpenAI-compatible servers such as LM Studio or llama.cpp, with document upload and semantic search via Qdrant. A Supply Depot offers a one-click app catalog and support for custom Docker containers, and opt-in automatic updates can be scheduled for the core software, apps, and content.
use_cases: Offline reference library on a home or field server
Chatting with a local AI model over private documents
Serving offline maps to devices on a local network
Classroom or family education server with multiple users
Running encryption or data-decoding tools in a browser offline
how_to_run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y curl && curl -fsSL -o install_nomad.sh && sudo bash install_nomad.sh
Advanced: copy the Docker Compose template from the README into docker-compose.yml, replace placeholders, then run: docker compose up -d
Update Command Center containers: sudo bash /opt/project-nomad/update_nomad.sh
Uninstall: curl -fsSL -o uninstall_nomad.sh && sudo bash uninstall_nomad.sh (cannot be undone)
notable: Fully offline after install; README states zero built-in telemetry and no internet needed except for install and optional downloads
Command Center orchestrates many containerized tools so users do not manage each one manually
Works with Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API server, including LM Studio and llama.cpp, for the AI Assistant
Opt-in auto-updates for minor/patch versions with a dry-run Ace command to test the decision logic without updating
Lightweight core (about 5 GB disk, under 1 GB RAM); the AI Assistant and content drive resource needs up
caveats: No authentication built in; the README advises against exposing it directly to the internet and recommends network-level controls
Debian-based systems only for the quick install; Windows users are pointed to a community-supported WSL2 path
The AI Assistant brings the install to roughly 25 GB, and optimal specs call for a GPU and 32 GB RAM; full content can require 250 GB or more
